description: Hi! I'm Andualem Genetu (Engineer AnduTechLab) from Ethiopia, competing solo for Challenge #7: Field Shift with "Andualem Smart AI Farm Hub." Built with Kotlin/Jetpack Compose, Node.js, and ESP32 IoT sensors (soil moisture, temp/humidity, ultrasonic water level, automated Blynk relay),Solar System, my bilingual (English/Amharic) offline-capable app fuses live field telemetry with NASA POWER, MERRA-2, MODIS NDVI, and GPM data for evidence-based crop rotation and irrigation advisories Using Voice.
summary:
Andualem Smart AI Farm Hub is a bilingual (English and Amharic) Android, Node.js, and ESP32 IoT platform built for Challenge #7: Field Shift — Adapting Farms with NASA Data.
We developed an end-to-end decision-support system that fuses live ground sensor telemetry (soil moisture, air temperature, humidity, ultrasonic water-tank level, and automated irrigation pump relay control via Blynk) with open NASA Earth observation datasets: NASA POWER agro-climatology, MERRA-2 surface and root-zone soil wetness (GWETTOP/GWETROOT), MODIS Terra 8-day NDVI vegetation imagery via NASA GIBS, and GPM precipitation data. Our Crop Rotation & Irrigation Decision Engine analyzes these signals to recommend resilient crop-shifting schedules, irrigation triggers, and soil health actions—complete with transparent data-confidence scoring and offline-capable schematic map fallbacks.
This matters because smallholder farmers in Ethiopia and similar regions lack costly laboratory probes and struggle with unpredictable weather shifts. Combining free NASA satellite intelligence with low-cost local sensors turns complex Earth science into practical, life-sustaining daily farming decisions.
details:
What It Does & How It Works

Andualem Smart AI Farm Hub is an end-to-end smart agriculture platform built for Challenge #7 (Field Shift: Adapting Farms with NASA Data). It bridges real-time IoT ground sensors with global NASA Earth observation datasets to help smallholder farmers adapt crop choices, irrigation schedules, and soil management to shifting climate conditions.

At the field level, an ESP32 microcontroller reads live environmental and soil conditions—soil moisture (V0), ambient temperature (V1), humidity (V2), ultrasonic water-tank level (V3), automated/manual pump relay status (V4/V11), and obstacle proximity (V12)—and streams them via Blynk IoT. Alongside this, a Node.js backend fetches and normalizes multi-source NASA datasets for the farm's coordinates (e.g., Bishoftu, Ethiopia):

1. NASA POWER Agro-climatology (temperature, solar irradiance, precipitation, and humidity trends)

2. MERRA-2 Soil Wetness (GWETTOP surface and GWETROOT root-zone wetness)

3. MODIS Terra 8-Day NDVI Vegetation Imagery via NASA GIBS WMTS

4. GPM (Global Precipitation Measurement) rainfall analytics

Inside the bilingual (English & Amharic) Android app, our Crop Rotation & Irrigation Decision Engine fuses live ESP32 ground readings with NASA satellite metrics to deliver actionable crop-shifting advisories, automated pump/irrigation recommendations, and transparent confidence levels (indicating whether advice is backed by full hardware + satellite data or partial/proxy inputs).

Benefits & Intended Impact

- Local Accessibility: Translates complex satellite science into clear, actionable guidance in both Amharic and English for Ethiopian and smallholder farmers.

- Water & Soil Conservation: Prevents over-irrigation by cross-checking local root moisture against MERRA-2 root-zone wetness and GPM rainfall trends, while recommending timely crop rotation to reduce soil exhaustion.

- Resilient Decision-Making Under Real Constraints: Built with an interactive offline-capable Schematic Map fallback and confidence-aware decision logic so rural farmers with limited internet or minimal sensor budgets still receive safe, trustworthy guidance.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

- Mobile App: Kotlin, Jetpack Compose (Material Design 3), Java legacy service interop, Gradle Kotlin DSL

- Testing & Verification: JUnit, Robolectric UI & decision-engine tests, Node.js integration tests (`node --test`)

- Backend & APIs: Node.js REST backend integrating NASA POWER, MERRA-2, MODIS GIBS WMTS, GPM, and Blynk Cloud APIs

- Hardware & Firmware: ESP32, Arduino IDE (C++), Blynk IoT, soil moisture sensor, DHT temperature/humidity sensor, ultrasonic tank sensor, irrigation pump relay module (with a Phase-2 architecture ready for RS485 NPK/pH probes)

Creativity & Key Design Considerations

1. Zero-Budget Soft-Sensing Proxy + Honest Confidence Scoring: Because industrial RS485 NPK/pH probes are too expensive for most smallholder farmers, our system computes transparent soft-sensing nutrient proxies from available moisture, climate, and satellite signals—while explicitly disclosing confidence levels rather than presenting estimates as direct lab measurements.

2. Small-Screen & Rural Usability: Engineered for compact mobile displays (360dp+ layouts), bilingual Amharic/English switching, and graceful offline/schematic map fallbacks.

3. Hardware Extensibility: Preserves full compatibility with existing low-cost ESP32 hardware today while offering a seamless upgrade path to physical NPK/pH probes as funding becomes available.
